 Maryland voters decide races for governor, attorney general, comptroller, Congress

 Maryland voters decide races for governor, attorney general, comptroller, Congress
 Greg Ng Digital Content Manager Blair Young Digital Content Producer Julian Nazario Digital Content Producer BALTIMORE — Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesday. WBAL-TV 11 News is your home for 2026 election coverage from across Maryland. Refresh this page often as updates come into the 11 Newsroom . 
 || Where to vote | Ballot drop box locations | What's on the ballot ||
 Advertisement 'It's been a wild ride' preparing Maryland's election
 Maryland State Elections Administrator Jared DeMarinis reflected on the work and the challenges the state met while preparing for the election.
 "It's been a wild ride, a little unprecedented at points. We're preparing. We've got all the equipment. We've got the judges trained. It looks like a great day," DeMarinis told WBAL-TV 11 News. "Go vote, period. Don't let anybody take away your right to vote. It's important."
 DeMarinis said he is pleased with the early voting turnout, which includes 124,000 votes cast on the last day of early voting alone, making it one of the highest turnout days in the state's history for early voting.
 "Go vote, period. Don't let anybody take away your right to vote. It's important."
 According to unofficial numbers from the state, more than 604,396 people voted over the eight-day early voting period. Now, the focuses shifts to Election Day on Tuesday.
 11 TV Hill video below: What voters need to know for Election Day 2026 
 "I want to see 100% voter turnout overall. So, I want to see everyone come out and vote. I'm always planning for that, but we plan for every contingency out there to create safe environments for voters," DeMarinis told WBAL-TV 11 News. "We worry about everything, and we've table-topped all those exercises and have contingency plans upon contingency plans."
 What happens after Election Day
 For Marylanders voting by mail, DeMarinis said the ballot needs to be returned on or before 8 p.m. on Election Day. He strongly suggests using an election drop box over sending it via the U.S. Postal Service.
 After Election Day, the first day to certify results is Nov. 13. Then, the state certifies the election on Dec. 3. Even after that, two post-election audits take place to check for accuracy.
 Video below: Why officials adviseagainst the mailbox for mail-in ballots 
 "We do a risk-limiting audit, which is considered the gold standard of auditing, and then, we also (send) digital images of all the scanned ballots to an independent provider and they calculate it on their software to see the results," DeMarinis told WBAL-TV 11 News.
 What's on the Maryland ballot
 Maryland voters are deciding top-level statewide leadership offices, including a rematch from 2022 as Democratic incumbent Gov. Wes Moore again faced off against Republican Dan Cox.
 Other statewide races include attorney general and comptroller, as well as three statewide ballot referendum questions, the third of which garnered the most discussion for what some considered was confusing language .
 "I want to see 100% voter turnout overall. So, I want to see everyone come out and vote."
 All eight of Maryland's Congressional districts were up for election, including in the open 5th District, where longtime Democratic incumbent Rep. Steny Hoyer announced his retirement in January . In June's Primary Election , Adrian Boafo emerged from a field of 24 Democrats and Chris Chaffee beat out two other Republicans to face off in the general election to succeed the 86-year-old former House majority leader.
 In the Baltimore area, there were races for county executive in all but Carroll County, and all five counties held races for County Council\Commissioners seats. And, this was the first year in which Baltimore County voters decided nine races for the expanded County Council.
